issues.display_title: Issue #349: Implement username deduplication in MentionPost worker
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 11/06/26

? Implementation Complete ? Ready for Unit Testing

Overview

Implement a duplicate-username elimination (deduplication) layer for mention-based notifications inside the Background Worker (src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost.go).

When a user is mentioned more than once in a single context (post or comment) ? e.g. "ipeb, lundara, ipeb" ? the system must send only one notification and create only one mention record per unique user.

Problem Statement

Previously every entry in the comma-separated recipientUsername string was processed, causing duplicate DB entries and multiple push notifications to the same user for the same event.

Design Decision: Worker-Side Processing

Deduplication is performed in the Background Worker (not the API) to keep API response time low and consistent, align with the existing asynchronous RabbitMQ delivery flow, and centralize username?userID resolution + block-list checks in one place right before notification logic.

Implementation Details

In src/Worker/MentionPost/MentionPost.go, on receiving a mention payload:

  1. Split the recipientUsername comma-separated string into a raw slice.
  2. Deduplicate using a map[string]bool to track seen usernames.
  3. Sanitize each username by trimming whitespace; skip empty entries.
  4. Rebuild a unique slice used for all subsequent DB lookups and notification broadcasts.
rawMentions := strings.Split(recipientUsername, ",")
uniqueMap := make(map[string]bool)
arrayMentions := []string{}
for _, m := range rawMentions {
    m = strings.TrimSpace(m)
    if m != "" && !uniqueMap[m] {
        uniqueMap[m] = true
        arrayMentions = append(arrayMentions, m)
    }
}

Acceptance Criteria

  • Duplicate usernames in a single mention event produce exactly one notification per unique user.
  • Whitespace is trimmed; empty entries (trailing/double commas) are skipped.
  • Only unique mention records are written to the database.
  • Block-list and username?userID resolution still work correctly after dedup.
  • API response time remains unaffected (dedup happens worker-side).

?? Testing Scenario (for Tester)

Scenario 1 ? Duplicate elimination

  1. Create a post/comment mentioning the same user multiple times: "ipeb, lundara, ipeb".
  2. Verify ipeb receives only ONE notification (not two).
  3. Verify lundara still receives their notification normally.
  4. Check the DB ? confirm only one mention record per unique user per event.
  • Expected: No duplicate DB entries, no duplicate push notifications.

Scenario 2 ? Whitespace & empty-entry sanitization

  1. Submit mentions with irregular spacing/commas: " ipeb , lundara , , ipeb,".
  2. Verify only ipeb and lundara are processed (no empty/blank recipients).
  3. Verify " ipeb" and "ipeb" are treated as the same user (trim works).
  • Expected: Exactly 2 unique notifications; no errors from empty strings.

Scenario 3 ? Block-list & resolution integrity

  1. Mention a user who has blocked the author, multiple times in one event.
  2. Verify the block is honored ? no notification is sent to that user.
  3. Mention a mix of valid, duplicate, and blocked users in one event.
  • Expected: Each valid unique user gets exactly one notification; blocked users get none.

Scenario 4 ? Regression & performance (redundant input)

  1. Submit a post with a large mention list containing many duplicates (e.g. 50 entries, 5 unique).
  2. Measure API response time ? should remain low/consistent (dedup is worker-side).
  3. Verify only 5 notifications and 5 DB records result.
  • Expected: Stable API latency, correct dedup, no DB query explosion.

issues.display_title: Issue #338: Worker: Location Grouping (async spatial + place_id matching)
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 09/06/26

? Implementation Complete ? Ready for Unit Testing

Implementation :

Overview

Dedicated asynchronous worker that handles all spatial and grouping logic off the post-publishing critical path, with improved accuracy via Google Place ID matching.

File: src/Worker/LocationGrouping/LocationGrouping.go
Queue: {PREFIX}_location_grouping

Problem

  • Spatial grouping must run async to keep publishing fast.
  • Coordinate drift between the location_post JSON and standalone latitude/longitude columns causes slug fragmentation (distance computed from 0,0 when columns are empty).
  • Minor coordinate variations for the same physical location can wrongly trigger new group creation.

Scope

  • Consume {PREFIX}_location_grouping; fetch the post's location data by post_id.
  • ResolveLocationGroup logic:
    • Place ID match: same Google place_id ? same group, regardless of coordinate drift or column status.
    • Empty-column fallback: when standalone coords are 0, default to exact name matching within the same vicinity (prevents slug fragmentation).
    • Haversine 15km as secondary check for custom locations without a place_id.
  • JSON-to-column sync: extract latitude/longitude from location_post JSON and update the posts columns.
  • Update location_group + location_group_slug on the post.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Posts sharing the same place_id are assigned to the same group.
  • Empty coordinate columns no longer match against 0,0.
  • latitude/longitude are backfilled to the posts columns from JSON.
  • Slug fragmentation for identical locations is eliminated.

Scenario Testing (for tester)

Pre-conditions: Worker process running and consuming {PREFIX}_location_grouping; ability to publish test messages and inspect the posts table.

  1. Place ID match grouping
    • Enqueue two post_ids with the same place_id but coords ~hundreds of meters apart.
    • Expected: both get the SAME location_group + location_group_slug.
  2. Empty standalone columns + JSON coords
    • Enqueue a post with latitude/longitude = 0.0 and valid coords in location_post JSON.
    • Expected: worker syncs coords from JSON into the columns; grouping uses real coords, not 0,0.
  3. Exact name fallback (no usable coords)
    • Enqueue a post with empty coords but a name matching an existing nearby group.
    • Expected: assigned to the existing group (no new slug).
  4. Haversine 15km secondary check (custom location, no place_id)
    • Enqueue two posts without place_id: one within 15km of an existing group, one beyond 15km.
    • Expected: the near one joins the existing group; the far one creates a new group.
  5. New unique slug creation
    • Enqueue a genuinely new location.
    • Expected: a new, unique location_group_slug is generated.
  6. Idempotency / re-processing
    • Re-enqueue the same post_id.
    • Expected: stable group assignment (no duplicate group, no slug churn).
  7. Malformed / missing post
    • Enqueue a non-existent post_id or malformed payload.
    • Expected: worker handles gracefully (logs + skips/nacks), does not crash or block the queue.

Pass criteria: All acceptance criteria verified; DB shows correct group/slug + backfilled coords; queue keeps draining without stalls.
